newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue-chips end down on currency, Telekom woes.
newsitem.headline: KL blue-chips end down on currency, Telekom woes.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks closed lower on continuing fears of currency volatility, rising interbank rates and slower growth at Telekom Malaysia, analysts said.
The benchmark Composite Index closed 11.90 points, or 1.16 percent, lower to 1,012.84.
"The expected strengthening of the local currency is somewhat faltering and interest rates are edging upwards," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage house.
"Telekom is definitely a factor," said a dealer at a local brokerage house.
Telekom closed 25 cents down to 9.70 ringgit, after dipping to a new 1997 low of 9.65 ringgit earlier.
Analysts had predicted a slower earnings growth for Telekom in the first half of 1997. It's financial results are expected on Friday.
The ringgit was weaker on Thursday, trading at 2.6310 against the U.S. dollar at around 0800 GMT. It closed at 2.6250 in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
Overnight interbank rates were around 8.80 percent, while the three-month was quoted at 8.45/50 percent, both trending upwards, analysts said.
Automotive stocks were hit by the general negative sentiments in the market, despite the release of strong first half vehicle sales data earlier in the day.
Proton, Diversified Resources and Tan Chong fell between four and 20 cents.
Sales of vehicles for the first six months of 1997 grew by 22.7 percent compared to the same period in 1996, said the Malaysian Motor Traders Association on Thursday.
Hong Leong Properties ended lower despite announcing a 29 percent gain in earnings for the year to June 30 on Thursday. The stock closed four cents down to 2.70 ringgit.
Overall market volume stood at 243 million shares, valued at 1,490 million ringgit, with 126 gainers and 506 losers.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the July spot contract slipped 10.2 points to 1,023.0 on its last day of trading, with 356 lots having changed hands. September futures dipped 21.0 points to 1,027.0 with 874 lots traded.
